amendments.rule: Where **one Greek noun** is rendered by an English adjective-plus-noun phrase, rule 17's head turns on whether the English **noun** is itself a gloss of the lexeme or a supplied generic completion. Where the noun glosses it, the noun is the head: `εὐδοκία` → *good pleasure*, `εὐνοία` → *good will*, `εὐαγγέλιον` → *good tidings*, `ζῷον` → *living creature*, `ἀρχιερεύς` → *chief priest* and *high priest*, `κτίσμα` → *created thing*, `ἀποκαραδοκία` → *earnest expectation*. Where it is a generic completion and another word carries the sense, that word is the head: `πλεονέκτης` → *covetous man* heads on *covetous*, as `ἀγάπαις` → *love feasts* heads on *love*, `πραιτώριον` → *praetorian guard* on *praetorian*, and `σπουδή` → *earnest care* on *earnest*, the corpus glossing that lexeme *diligence* and never *care*. This is rule 17's generic-noun clause holding for a noun rather than a substantival adjective or demonstrative, and the same test it already applies to `all things` and `good thing`. Do not decide it from English syntax: rule 17 forbids choosing a word merely because it is the phrase's formal head, which is the only thing *care* or *man* could rely on. The phrase need not be adjective-plus-noun for this test, and the ASV's word order does not change it. Where the ASV renders one Greek **compound** word — a noun or a verb — by two English words **each of which glosses one of its elements**, the head is the word answering to the compound's **core** and not the one answering to its modifying, incorporated or prefixed element, even where English syntax makes that modifier the phrase's formal head and puts the core in a complement: `πιθανολογίᾳ` → *persuasiveness of speech* heads on *speech* and `ἐθελοθρησκίᾳ` → *will worship* on *worship*, as rule 91's `καταλαλιάς` → *evil speakings* heads on *speakings* and `δυσφημίας` → *evil report* on *report*, and as rule 104's `εὐπειθής` → *easy to be entreated* and `εὐάρεστος` → *well pleasing* head their stem words. A compound **verb** is decided the same way and its core is the **verbal** element, so `καρποφοροῦντες` → *bearing fruit* heads on *bearing* and `εἰρηνοποιήσας` → *having made peace* on *made*, the incorporated `καρπο-` and `εἰρηνο-` being the modifying element however plainly the English noun reads as the phrase's complement. Rule 17's *make straight* and rule 91's *make known*, *make request* and *bear witness* are untouched and are the contrast, decided by rule 91's own test: there no part of the English verb glosses the lexeme, `εὐθύνω`, `γνωρίζω`, `αἰτέω` and `μαρτυρέω` each carrying a single root whose sense the English complement alone spells. A **denominal** verb formed from one root with a causative or verbalizing suffix is that case and not this one, which is why `ἱκανώσαντι` → *made … meet* still heads on *meet*, and rule 104 is untouched for the same reason, `φλογίζω` → *setteth on fire* heading on *fire* because *setteth* answers to no element of it. That is this rule's own line held to and not an exception to it: `εὐδοκία`, `εὐνοία` and `εὐαγγέλιον` all head the core and never the `εὐ-`. So ask first whether **both** English words gloss something, and only then which of them is the core; where one of them glosses no element at all the generic-completion arm decides it instead, which is why *man* and *feasts* lose to *covetous* and *love*. Rule 46 is untouched, because `χάριν` is a postposition rather than a noun and the supplied *cause* or *sake* is what carries its sense, and rules 22, 49 and 58 are untouched, because there the supplied word answers to an article or determines a phrase rather than completing a noun's own English expression.
amendments.why: Rule 66's compound arm was written for a compound noun, and COL.1 met it three times with compound verbs — karpophoreo twice and eirenopoieo once. Read as scoped to nouns, the rule left rule 17's make-plus-complement clause governing the verb case, which is how COL.1.20 came to head having made peace on peace while COL.1.6 and COL.1.10 headed bearing fruit on bearing. The amendment widens the arm to a compound word of either class, names the verbal core as the head for a compound verb, and fences it against the two neighbouring cases the corpus already settles the other way: a single-root verb whose English complement carries the whole sense (rule 91's make known and bear witness, rule 17's make straight) and a denominal causative (ikanoo -> made meet), neither of which has an English verb word that glosses an element. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because the over-broad word was the single term 'noun' inside rule 66's own sentence, and a cross-reference would have left it standing for whoever read that rule first.

conventions: A Greek compound word rendered by two English words each of which glosses one of its elements heads on the core, and for a compound verb the core is the verbal element: karpophoreo -> bearing fruit heads on bearing at COL.1.6 and COL.1.10, and eirenopoiesas -> having made peace heads on made at COL.1.20, where the reconciliation pass corrected a head on peace. The contrast in this chapter is a verb whose English complement carries the whole lexical sense because no part of the English verb glosses the lexeme - gnorisai -> to make known on known (COL.1.27), aitoumenoi -> make request on request (COL.1.9), and the denominal causative ikanosanti -> made ... meet on meet (COL.1.12).

In aph' hes hemeras -> since the day (COL.1.6, COL.1.9) the relative pronoun takes the English 'the', occupying the determiner slot of the noun it governs, and hemeras stands bare. The competing reading - 'the' as a rule 7 helper on the noun with the relative left unrepresented - is named in both units' notes; the chapter takes the relative throughout.

report: One real cross-verse split: a Greek compound verb rendered by an English verb plus noun was headed on the verbal core at COL.1.6 and COL.1.10 (karpophoreo -> bearing fruit, head 'bearing') and on the incorporated nominal element at COL.1.20 (eirenopoiesas -> having made peace, head 'peace'). Identical construction, nothing in the source licensing the difference. Patched COL.1.20 to head on 'made'; COL.1.6 and COL.1.10 already read that way and are untouched.

The deciding rule is 66's compound arm, which heads a compound on its core and not on its modifying or prefixed element (ethelothreskia -> will worship on worship). Rule 91's empty-support-verb contrast does not reach eirenopoieo: 'made' glosses -poieo, whereas 'make' in make known (COL.1.27) and make request (COL.1.9) glosses nothing, and ikanosanti -> made ... meet (COL.1.12) is a denominal causative with a single root and rightly stays headed on 'meet'.

Candidates checked and rejected as splits: the two kathos clauses in COL.1.6 differ exactly as rule 82's written-word test requires (even as ... also / as ... also) and COL.1.7's bare kathos keeps even as whole; articular ta panta splits under rule 102 while anarthrous panton/pasin keeps all things whole under rule 17, COL.1.17 writing both in one verse; rule 20's two arms are applied by the presence of a possessor token, COL.1.24 writing both; the single English 'for' over two apo at COL.1.26 (rule 36) and the doubled 'of' over one licensing token at COL.1.4 (rule 103) are mirror cases; every two-word English preposition heads on the prepositional word (because of, according to, out of, on behalf, for sake, to ward).

Read end to end for the added/folded asymmetry the lemma table is blind to. The three added units are of the Father (COL.1.19), I say (COL.1.20) and the appositional even (COL.1.26), each a case rules 5, 103 and 105 separate from a fold; supplied pronouns (it at 1.9 and 1.26, us at 1.13) fold onto the verb that licenses them throughout, and supplied determiners go to anarthrous nouns under rule 51's anarthrous clause at 1.1, 1.3, 1.8, 1.15 and 1.18 without exception.

BSB: all ten disagreements are ASV-unrepresented articles under rule 20 displacement (1.9, 1.20, 1.22, 1.26 tois), rule 31's second attributive article (1.12 toi, 1.23, 1.26 to) and rule 21/23's determinerless phrase (1.12 ten and toi, 1.27). These are the documented convention difference and none is a genuine error; nothing was changed to move the rate.

Two conventions recorded and one amendment returned to rule 66. No corpus request needed: rule 66's compound arm decides the head on the contract's own terms and the chapter supplies three units of it.
